narrative:
The model estimates a 45% chance that you will leave your job. This moderate risk is high enough that the company has decided to deny your promotion, as they are concerned about investing in someone who might not stay long-term.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key factors. Most influential was that you have not received any other job offers while working here. This actually pushes the model toward expecting you to stay, because most employees who are predicted to remain also report no external opportunities. Your relatively short overall career experience of 1-5 years was the second strongest factor and works in the opposite direction, pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have such limited experience, while more seasoned colleagues tend to be seen as more stable. Finally, you find it difficult to get involved in decision-making and have your opinions heard at work. This lack of engagement is the third most important driver and strongly pushes the prediction toward you leaving. Most employees expected to stay describe their involvement as medium or easy.

Taken together, your limited experience and low job involvement outweighed the stabilizing effect of having no other offers, leading to the decision against promotion. The organization should discuss ways to increase your voice in decisions and explore clearer career paths. You may want to reflect on whether this role truly matches your long-term goals.
